name: SMERC
category: recoverability-aware runtime permission infrastructure for AI agents, MCP tool calls, GitHub Actions, cloud automation, financial-action workflows, and high-impact automated systems
mission: SMERC helps intelligent systems make safer decisions before irreversible actions occur, so people and organizations can trust the technology shaping their lives.
one_line_summary: SMERC checks whether a technically authorized action is recoverable enough to execute now, then returns a replayable posture: ALLOW, THROTTLE, FREEZE, DENY, or ESCALATE.
reviewer_summary: SMERC is a pilot-grade technical artifact for testing recoverability before execution. It complements identity, authorization, policy engines, AI gateways, sandboxes, approval workflows, and audit logs by adding a pre-execution question: if this action is allowed, is it recoverable, bounded, supported by trusted evidence, and safe to proceed right now?

primary_wedge.name: GitHub Actions shadow-mode governance
primary_wedge.description: Score AI-assisted code, deployment, infrastructure, permission, and workflow actions before execution while existing controls remain authoritative.
primary_wedge.why_this_first: It is easy for a reviewer to understand, can be tested with metadata-only actions, and exposes the difference between simple allow/block controls and recoverability-aware middle states.

implemented_surfaces: SPARTa execution routing and control translation
Recovery Authority Gate for governed unlock after pause
complete lifecycle proof connecting admission, pause, unlock, permit, execution result, and ledger evidence
postcondition evidence comparing SPARTa-required controls with observed control, execution, hold, and rollback evidence
customer-owned metadata request for asking external reviewers to replace public examples with safe action metadata
cloud-admin proof pack with cloud reason codes
cloud metadata connector for read-only change exports
public benchmark ingestion pack for agent-governance, MCP-security, action-boundary, consequence, cloud, and financial benchmark-shaped examples
serious report performance evidence for local p50, p95, and maximum proof-path latency

current_evidence.evidence_boundary: Synthetic examples, public-pattern benchmark scenarios, local reports, and public technical review are not the same as customer validation, production certification, incident-reduction proof, or willingness-to-pay proof.

recommended_review_sequence.name: Read the public review snapshot
recommended_review_sequence.result: Reviewer understands what exists, what changed recently, and what should not be believed yet.

recommended_review_sequence.name: Read the company reviewer front door
recommended_review_sequence.result: Reviewer chooses the shortest path: general customer evaluation, cloud-admin evaluation, financial runtime evaluation, or complete lifecycle proof.

recommended_review_sequence.name: Run the complete lifecycle proof
recommended_review_sequence.result: Reviewer sees the connected lifecycle: ADMIT -> FREEZE -> PAUSE -> UNLOCK -> THROTTLE -> CONSTRAINED_EXECUTE -> permit verified -> execution succeeded -> ledger valid.

recommended_review_sequence.name: Inspect the public action governance benchmark
recommended_review_sequence.result: Reviewer sees where SMERC differs from simple allow/deny across metadata-only action scenarios.

recommended_review_sequence.name: Run the postcondition evidence report
recommended_review_sequence.result: Reviewer sees whether SPARTa-required controls were actually observed after routing, including pass, gap, violation, and unobserved statuses.

recommended_review_sequence.name: Run the public benchmark ingestion pack
recommended_review_sequence.result: Reviewer sees how representative public agent-governance, MCP, action-boundary, consequence, cloud, and financial benchmark-shaped examples map into SMERC posture, SPARTa routes, and DLL evidence without claiming official benchmark scores.

recommended_review_sequence.name: Run the serious report performance harness
recommended_review_sequence.result: Reviewer sees local proof-path p50, p95, and maximum timing for serious reports without treating local timing as production SLA evidence.

recommended_review_sequence.name: Generate the customer-owned metadata request
recommended_review_sequence.result: Reviewer receives a safe ask for replacing public examples with 5 to 25 metadata-only actions from one real workflow.

recommended_review_sequence.name: Run the pilot-in-a-box path
recommended_review_sequence.result: Reviewer receives a local proof package across general AI-agent, cloud-admin, financial-runtime, and single-action examples.

recommended_review_sequence.name: Replace examples with 5 to 25 safe company-owned metadata records
recommended_review_sequence.result: Reviewer can test whether SMERC changes judgment on actions that resemble their own workflows without sharing secrets or production authority.

recommended_review_sequence.name: Run the Financial Runtime evaluation when the workflow is financial
recommended_review_sequence.result: Financial-services reviewers can test metadata-only payment, refund, treasury, stablecoin, tokenized-collateral, wallet-policy, transaction-limit, and reserve-status actions.

recommended_review_sequence.name: Decide whether a bounded shadow-mode pilot is justified
recommended_review_sequence.result: Reviewer has a concrete go/no-go gate before any live integration discussion.

non_claims: SMERC is not proven to reduce live incidents.
SMERC is not customer-validated for willingness to pay.
SMERC is not a replacement for IAM, OPA, AI gateways, sandboxes, SIEM, SOAR, EDR, GRC, code review, approval workflows, or human accountability.
SMERC should not silently retrain itself or automatically activate policy changes from ledger learning records.
best_next_external_question: Does recoverability before execution change reviewer judgment enough to justify a shadow-mode pilot on real workflow metadata?
best_next_build_question: Can a company replace the example actions with its own safe metadata in under 30 minutes and receive a useful go/no-go pilot report?
